response.title: What size lithium battery do I need to run an 80 lb trolling motor all day, including holding the boat in place in wind?
response.answer:
For an 80 lb thrust trolling motor, I recommend a 24V 150Ah to 200Ah LiFePO4 lithium battery system if you want to fish all day (8–10 hours), including using Spot-Lock or anchor mode to hold your boat in wind.

If you regularly fish in strong wind, I'd lean toward 24V 200Ah for the extra reserve.

Battery size recommendations

Most 80 lb trolling motors run on 24V, including many Minn Kota and MotorGuide models.

markup:
For an **80 lb thrust trolling motor**, I recommend a **24V 150Ah to 200Ah LiFePO4 lithium battery system** if you want to fish all day (8–10 hours), including using Spot-Lock or anchor mode to hold your boat in wind.

If you regularly fish in strong wind, I'd lean toward **24V 200Ah** for the extra reserve.

## Battery size recommendations

Most 80 lb trolling motors run on 24V, including many Minn Kota and MotorGuide models.

| Battery setup | Energy capacity | Recommendation |
|---|---:|---|
| 24V 50Ah | 1,280Wh | Light use, calm water |
| 24V 100Ah | 2,560Wh | Moderate all-day fishing |
| 24V 150Ah | 3,840Wh | All-day fishing with wind |
| 24V 200Ah | 5,120Wh | Best for long days and windy conditions |

## Estimated runtime

An 80 lb trolling motor typically draws approximately 50–60 amps at full power on a 24V system. That's roughly 1,200–1,440 watts.

Here are approximate runtimes assuming 90% usable battery capacity.

| Average motor draw | 24V 100Ah | 24V 150Ah | 24V 200Ah |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 10A — light use | 9 hr | 13.5 hr | 18 hr |
| 20A — moderate wind | 4.5 hr | 6.8 hr | 9 hr |
| 30A — strong wind | 3 hr | 4.5 hr | 6 hr |
| 50A — heavy load | 1.8 hr | 2.7 hr | 3.6 hr |

These are illustrative estimates, not guaranteed runtimes. Spot-Lock consumption varies considerably with wind, current, boat size, and how often the motor needs to correct position.

## My recommendation

Make sure the battery's BMS supports your motor's maximum current draw, preferably with at least a 60A continuous discharge rating at 24V, subject to the motor manufacturer's specifications.

        <radio value="10–15 mph">10–15 mph</radio>
        <radio value="15–20 mph">15–20 mph</radio>
        <radio value="Over 20 mph">Over 20 mph</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <divider color="subtle"/>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>3. How long do you want to stay on the water?</label>

        <radio value="10–12 hours">10–12 hours</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <button block submit>Calculate my battery size <icon name="arrow-right" inline/></button>
  </form>
</box>

With those details, I can narrow it down to whether **100Ah, 150Ah, or 200Ah** makes the most sense without spending unnecessarily on battery capacity.
